maPrimeRenov2026.status: As of 2026-10-14, MaPrimeRénov' 'par geste' in metropolitan France no longer funds any insulation work. Since 2026-09-01 the par-geste forfaits only cover air/water heat pumps, geothermal or solar-thermal heat pumps, and connection to a heating or cooling network. A non-mandatory energy audit (only with a works item) and removal of an oil tank are also still covered. Wall insulation (ITE/ITI) was dropped earlier, on 2026-01-01. Between 2026-01-01 and 2026-08-31 the only insulation items left par geste were rampants/plafonds de combles and toitures-terrasses. Insulation is still financed under MaPrimeRénov' rénovation d'ampleur, and by CEE.

timeline.event: Wall insulation (ITE and ITI) and biomass boilers are no longer financed under MaPrimeRénov' par geste.

Anah application portals reopened for all routes and all households once the loi de finances 2026 was promulgated. They had been on hold with files pending since late 2025. The 2026 budget for MaPrimeRénov' is 3.6 billion euros (at least 120,000 rénovations d'ampleur and 150,000 par geste).
timeline.note: The exact reopening date was not verified from a primary source. A secondary commercial source (vasco-impact.com, seen only in a search summary) gives 23 February 2026, so treat that date as low confidence. The Anah guide also says rénovation d'ampleur became 'de nouveau accessible à tous les ménages' after the budget passed, which implies it had been restricted in late 2025. Details of the 2025 suspension were not verified in this session.

Par-geste forfaits are refocused on heat pumps. Forfaits for insulation, ventilation and other heating systems are withdrawn, except connection to a heating network. Rénovation d'ampleur in single-family houses can no longer keep or install gas or oil heating.

dom.note: RT2012/RE2020 and their H1a–H3 zoning cover metropolitan France only (the RE2020 arrêté is titled '... en France métropolitaine'; the 3CL table lists only the 96 metropolitan départements). New housing in Guadeloupe, Martinique, Guyane and La Réunion is governed by the RTAA DOM (Réglementation thermique, acoustique et aération, revised 2016); per the ministry, the RTAA 2016 thermal arrêté applies only in Guyane and La Réunion, and Mayotte is excluded from the acoustic/ventilation arrêtés. Some consumer sites (e.g. Hellowatt) place 971–976 in 'H3' for CEE purposes; treat as unverified. The RTAA DOM 2016 brochure gives requirements mostly as solar factors (e.g. opaque roofs S ≤ 0.03, walls S ≤ 0.09) with U-value limits only for La Réunion above 600 m (horizontal opaque walls/roofs U ≤ 0.5 W/m²·K, vertical U ≤ 2 W/m²·K) — i.e. the DOM logic is anti-heat rather than winter insulation. Recommendation for the calculator: do not offer H1a–H3 targets for DOM; show a notice instead.

conventions.calculationMethod: Steady-state method of Th-Bat 2020 fascicule Parois opaques (formulas 225–226; NF EN ISO 6946 is a Th-Bat normative reference) and Th-U Ex (formulas 2–3): each homogeneous layer R_i = e_i / λ_i (e in m, measured as installed; λ = useful conductivity from fascicule Matériaux); R_paroi = Σ R_i (+ air layers); U_c = 1 / (Rsi + R_paroi + Rse); U_p = U_c + ΔU (integrated thermal bridges such as studs, joists, fixings). Rsi/Rse depend on heat-flow direction (horizontal 0.13/0.04, upward 0.10/0.04, downward 0.17/0.04); for a wall, ceiling or floor adjoining an unheated space (garage, comble perdu, vide sanitaire) Rse = Rsi; layers outside a strongly ventilated air gap are ignored. Sizing added insulation: R_existing = Σ e_i/λ_i of existing layers (structure plus any existing insulation at its measured thickness, with a conservative λ for old products); R_to_add = max(0, R_target − R_existing); thickness = R_to_add × λ_new (m); for loose fill divide that thickness by (1 − s). If the target is a U value: R_to_add = 1/U_target − (Rsi + Rse) − R_existing. Convention: the RT existant minimum R (arrêté du 3 mai 2007, as reproduced in the Guide DPE v3) is "R de l’ensemble paroi + isolant" (Rsi/Rse excluded), so the structure’s own R may count toward it; aid schemes may instead require the R of the added insulation alone (not verified here). For bare existing walls/floors/ceilings without layer detail, the 3CL-DPE U0 tables can be used: R_structure ≈ 1/U0 − (Rsi + Rse) (derived; conventional values).

prices.vatNote: Retail prices are TTC as displayed to private buyers (standard TVA 20 % on DIY material purchases; Brico Dépôt also adds the éco-participation inside TTC where applicable). Installed (pose comprise) prices are those published by guides/brokers; most say 'TTC' or 'pose comprise' without stating which VAT rate is embedded. Insulation works invoiced by a professional on a dwelling completed more than 2 years ago qualify for the reduced TVA of 5,5 % (cited by Maison Saint-Gobain, Construires, Effy, Hello Watt); DIY material bought at retail does not. Aid context (single commercial sources, NOT verified against france-renov.gouv.fr): Construires.fr states ITE/ITI left MaPrimeRénov' 'par geste' on 1 Jan 2026; Selectra (4 Sep 2026) states decree n° 2026-822 of 25 Aug 2026 removed insulation (incl. combles) from MaPrimeRénov' par geste for applications from 1 Sep 2026, leaving CEE, éco-PTZ, TVA 5,5 % and MaPrimeRénov' rénovation d'ampleur. Retail data quality: Brico Dépôt pages were read live on 2026-10-14 (high). Leroy Merlin (HTTP 403), Castorama (HTTP 503 'temporairement indisponible') and Point.P (Cloudflare challenge) could not be opened; their figures come from search-engine snippets of their own pages seen on 2026-10-14 (capture date of the snippet unknown unless noted) and are marked medium/low. existingMaterials.label_fr: Isolation présente mais épaisseur / résistance inconnues (règle 3CL-DPE)
existingMaterials.assumption: 3CL-DPE 2021: if insulation is present but neither R nor thickness is known, use the insulation year (if unknown: the construction year; if construction ≤ 1974 the insulation year is taken as 1975–1977) and set U = min(U_nu ; U_tab). If presence of insulation is unknown, U = min(U_nu ; U_tab) with the construction period (≤ 1974 → no insulation assumed: 2.5 / 2 / 2.5). Tables give U (W/m²·K) by period, climate zone (H1/H2/H3) and whether heating is electric Joule-effect.
existingMaterials.note: The Uph "terrasse" column also applies when the space above is unheated or non-residential. Values extracted from the consolidated annex (Oct 2021) and checked row by row against the ADEME observatoire valeur_tables.xlsx (sheets umur, upb, uph).

existingMaterials.label_fr: Isolation équivalente implicite des combles selon la période (dérivée du 3CL)
existingMaterials.assumption: Back-calculated from 3CL Uph_tab (combles, zone H1, non-Joule heating) with Uph0 = 2.5 (plafond plaque de plâtre): R_ins = 1/Uph_tab − 1/2.5; thickness at λ = 0.04.
existingMaterials.note: DERIVED, not stated by the source: these are the conventional equivalents implied by the DPE, not measured typical installed thicknesses (≈6.4 cm for 1975–1982, ≈11.7 cm for 1983–1988, ≈14.4 cm for 1989–2000). The commonly quoted "8–10 cm of glass wool in 1970s–80s attics" could not be verified from a primary source.

existingMaterials.label_fr: Laine minérale existante (âge, densité, humidité inconnus)
existingMaterials.assumption: Use the Th-U Ex default conductivity for insulation already in place, with the thickness measured on site.
existingMaterials.note: Th-U Ex fascicule 2/5 (2008) applies to products in buildings built after 1948 "en absence de données sur leur teneur en eau, leur masse volumique et l’impact du vieillissement". Same 0.04 for PSE and verre cellulaire; 0.03 for PU / XPS.

existingMaterials.label_fr: Laine de verre ancienne légère (rouleaux non certifiés)
existingMaterials.assumption: If density is low/unknown and the product is not certified, the Th-Bat default λ by density is more conservative than 0.04.
existingMaterials.note: The numbers are Th-Bat defaults for non-certified glass wool (high confidence as values); applying them to 1970s–80s products is our assumption (densities of that era not verified). Suggested range for old glass wool: 0.040 (Th-U Ex) to 0.047–0.055 (low density).

existingMaterials.label_fr: Laine de verre ancienne tassée / écrasée
existingMaterials.assumption: No official degradation factor found. Th-Bat defines R = e/λ with e measured as installed: measure the current (compressed) thickness and use it; do not use the original nominal thickness.
existingMaterials.note: Guide DPE v3 (2024): defects such as "isolant tassé ou mouillé" may be noted as comments but are NOT taken into account in the 3CL calculation; its work recommendations say to remove insulation in poor condition or badly installed before adding new insulation, and to remove earlier inadequate work when the conductivity of existing insulants is degraded. A numeric R-loss for compressed or wet wool could not be verified (ADEME / France Rénov pages were not accessible or silent on it).

existingMaterials.assumption: Treat as zero (remove and replace) rather than assigning a reduced λ.
existingMaterials.note: The Guide DPE recommends removal when algae/mould proliferate or conductivity is degraded. The factor 0 is our conservative app convention, not a stated value. Th-Bat only gives moisture corrections for XPS in inverted roofs (+2 to +4 mW/m·K), not for wet mineral wool.

existingMaterials.label_fr: Laine minérale soufflée en vrac sur plancher de combles
existingMaterials.assumption: R = e × (1 − s) / λ with settlement (tassement) s.
existingMaterials.note: Th-Bat §4.3.2 (formulas 267–268), table "Soufflage à la machine sur plancher plat"; same in Th-bat Parois opaques 2017. Manual pouring (déversement manuel, 30–60 kg/m³): s = 0.05, λ = 0.065.

existingMaterials.label_fr: Ouate de cellulose soufflée sur plancher de combles
Fibres de bois soufflées sur plancher de combles
existingMaterials.note: Same table: fibres de coton soufflées (10–20 kg/m³) s 0.35, λ 0.055; chanvre et lin soufflés (10–20) s 0.35, λ 0.058; chanvre et lin déversés (15–25) s 0.35, λ 0.060.
Loose vermiculite is found in some older attics (observation, not from the source).

existingMaterials.assumption: U = 1/(1/U_nu + e/0.04) for walls and high floors; 1/(1/Upb0 + e/0.042) for low floors; if R is known: U = 1/(1/U_nu + R).
existingMaterials.note: DPE convention; it ignores degradation (see Guide DPE).
